Title: Coloring molecules for Caco-2 cell permeability
Description: Estimates apparent permeability across a Caco-2 monolayer, the in vitro gold-standard proxy for how readily an orally dosed compound crosses the intestinal wall. Values come back as the negative log10 of Papp in cm/s, so a higher number means a less permeable compound. Jimenez-Luna and colleagues fitted a message-passing graph neural network, paired with integrated-gradients colouring of the atoms behind each prediction, to 239 compounds pooled from two studies. With so little data and a cross-validated Pearson R of 0.53, treat the output as a ranking aid.
Interpretation: Negative log10 of Caco-2 apparent permeability in cm/s, where lower values indicate greater permeability.
